key_insight: FREDI jointly optimizes fair wireless resource allocation and dual-threshold early-exit inference so secure edge intelligence can route only critical events for deeper edge-side classification.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives a practical optimization pipeline for deploying scalable, fair, and secure UE–edge–cloud inference under tight bandwidth, compute, and latency constraints.
method: Proportional-fair optimization of UE–ES association, bandwidth, transmit power, and processing resources.
Dual-threshold early-exit CNN screening with exact threshold search over the finite empirical confidence set.
Mixed-integer exponential-cone reformulation with pre-elimination of infeasible UE–ES pairs and certified global-optimality gap control.
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 report near-perfect fairness, utility close to a Sum-Utility benchmark, and Stage-A scalability from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve time below 0.1 s.
watch_item: The optimization is exact within a prescribed gap, but performance and solve time may depend on the empirical confidence distribution and problem size, especially when security constraints fragment resources.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
